[} Build AI-Powered Applications with MongoDB Atlas in Grok Build The rise of AI agents has fundamentally changed how software is built, with agentic platforms like Grok Build redefining the unit of software work. Instead of asking an AI assistant for a function, a developer or architect gives an autonomous agent a goal, constraints, a codebase, and a definition of done. The agent researches, proposes a plan, edits files, runs tests, and iterates. [} Code Mode Without the Interpreter: Agents That Write Aggregation Pipelines Standfirst Code mode gives an AI agent a code interpreter and lets it write real programs—one round trip instead of five, filtering where the data lives instead of in the context window. It also means running arbitrary code that a model wrote, which is a hard sell in a regulated product. This is an account of doing the same thing without the interpreter: the agent authors a MongoDB aggregation pipeline, a handler executes it server-side, and only the reshaped result crosses back. Two production systems, the query work that made them viable, and where the approach falls down. That shift raises the bar on what an agent needs underneath it.
